paragraphs.heading: 1\. VERIFIED OBSERVATIONS
paragraphs.text: The confirmation contained Google Meet URL https\://meet.google.com/wir-itbv-mbe. Calendar searches found no corresponding event in any of 11 connected calendars for the target time. paragraphs.heading: 1\. VERIFIED OBSERVATIONS

paragraphs.heading: 2\. RISK / CURRENT DECISION
paragraphs.text: A visitor may receive a “confirmed” booking email without the owner having a corresponding calendar appointment, creating a risk of missed meetings.

paragraphs.heading: 2\. RISK / CURRENT DECISION
paragraphs.text: Do not call booking fully production-ready until verified. Do not modify the live site or overwrite GitHub main without source verification and release QA.

paragraphs.heading: 3\. INVESTIGATION WHEN RESUMED
paragraphs.text: Inspect the exact booking handler, Google Apps Script executions and Cloud logs around 20 October 2026 16:11 UTC (21:11 PKT). Correlate the reference above with request, response, errors, and calendar event ID.

paragraphs.heading: 3\. INVESTIGATION WHEN RESUMED

paragraphs.heading: 3\. INVESTIGATION WHEN RESUMED

paragraphs.heading: 3\. INVESTIGATION WHEN RESUMED

4\. RECOMMENDED RELIABLE DESIGN

paragraphs.heading: 4\. RECOMMENDED RELIABLE DESIGN
paragraphs.text: Use an independent booking backend/database as source of truth, with appointment ID, UTC timestamps, original time zone, contact, state, external calendar ID, idempotency key, audit trail, and lead CRM association.

paragraphs.heading: 4\. RECOMMENDED RELIABLE DESIGN
paragraphs.text: Enforce server-side slot availability and transactional double-booking prevention. States: pending, confirmed, sync_failed, cancelled, rescheduled.

paragraphs.heading: 4\. RECOMMENDED RELIABLE DESIGN
paragraphs.text: Use a durable outbox/queue and idempotent workers for Calendar/Meet synchronization and email delivery; retry transient failures with exponential backoff and dead-letter handling. Distinguish internal reservation from externally confirmed calendar/Meet sync.

paragraphs.heading: 4\. RECOMMENDED RELIABLE DESIGN
paragraphs.text: Never send a “Calendar and Meet confirmed” email unless required external operations are verified. If sync fails, keep the reservation visible internally and alert the owner; offer a safe retry or fallback instead of silently losing a booking.

paragraphs.heading: 4\. RECOMMENDED RELIABLE DESIGN
paragraphs.text: Build a private calendar view inside the Lead CRM; Google Calendar and Google Meet remain optional external integrations. Implement monitoring, structured logs, alerts, reconciliation, and secure secrets management.

paragraphs.heading: 5\. RELEASE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

paragraphs.heading: Working name: Studio OS (provisional, subject to brand review)
paragraphs.text: Vision: Evolve the existing portfolio Leads Portal into a premium, reusable CMS + CRM + analytics + SEO + lead-generation platform. First connected website: hadi.intellignce.net. Future capability: connect multiple websites, including INTELLIGNCE or clients, without rebuilding the core.
PRODUCT GOALS

paragraphs.heading: PRODUCT GOALS
paragraphs.text: One secure workspace to understand where traffic originates, which content and campaigns generate qualified leads, how organic search performs, and which actions should happen next. Provide practical website content management, lead operations, booking, Sera AI oversight, and trustworthy reporting. Do not confuse site visits with identified people, or Google Search Console impressions with analytics sessions.
MODULES AND CAPABILITIES

paragraphs.heading: MODULES AND CAPABILITIES
paragraphs.text: A. Overview / Command Center: configurable KPI cards for sessions, engaged visitors, acquisition channels, conversions, qualified leads, booked calls, and pipeline value; trend comparisons; data freshness indicators; alerts and action queue.

paragraphs.heading: MODULES AND CAPABILITIES
paragraphs.text: B. CRM / Leads: unified lead records, deduplication, provenance and consent, attribution history, lifecycle stages, owner assignment, notes, tags, tasks, follow-ups, contact forms, email interactions, Sera AI conversations when appropriately disclosed, and booking status. Support export and deletion requests.

paragraphs.heading: MODULES AND CAPABILITIES
paragraphs.text: C. CMS / Content Studio: reusable page and case-study models, rich text and structured fields, media library, image optimization, draft/review/publish states, scheduled publishing, preview, version history, rollback, metadata and redirects. The CMS must not overwrite the original portfolio content during migration.

paragraphs.heading: MODULES AND CAPABILITIES
paragraphs.text: D. Traffic & Conversion Analytics: privacy-conscious event collection or integration with established analytics; acquisition channels, UTM campaigns, referral sources, landing pages, geographic aggregates, device classes, funnels, form submissions, AI interactions, and booking conversions. Apply bot filtering, retention rules, consent handling and aggregation. Anonymous events should not be retroactively linked to named leads without an appropriate lawful basis and clear user notice.

paragraphs.heading: MODULES AND CAPABILITIES
paragraphs.text: E. SEO Intelligence: Google Search Console integration for queries, clicks, impressions, average position, indexing/coverage where available; sitemap status, canonical and robots checks, technical crawl findings, page-specific metadata, internal links, and structured-data checks. Integrate PageSpeed Insights/CrUX where available for performance metrics. Clearly label sampled/estimated, delayed, and unavailable data. Off-page reporting may track backlinks, brand mentions, referral traffic, outreach opportunities and earned links, with source provenance; do not promise ranking or automate spam links.

paragraphs.heading: MODULES AND CAPABILITIES
paragraphs.text: F. Automations / Sera AI / Bookings: safe lead triage, approved notifications, email and calendar sync, meeting lifecycle, workflow builder, human approval gates for consequential actions, prompt/version controls, cost and usage limits, abuse safeguards, audit trails and failure alerts. Calendar confirmation must be verified; existing missing-calendar-event bug is a blocker for production booking claims.

paragraphs.heading: MODULES AND CAPABILITIES
paragraphs.text: G. Integrations / Site Connections: per-site API credentials with rotation, webhook signing, retry and replay controls, event schema versioning, SDK/embeddable capture where appropriate, OAuth connections for Google services, and optional MCP tools for governed AI-agent operations. MCP complements but does not replace a stable API and webhook layer.
REFERENCE ARCHITECTURE (PROPOSAL)

paragraphs.heading: REFERENCE ARCHITECTURE (PROPOSAL)
paragraphs.text: Premium responsive admin UI (Next.js/React) → authenticated backend/API → PostgreSQL (Supabase) with strict tenant/site isolation and row-level security where appropriate → background jobs/outbox for integrations → analytics aggregation pipeline → audit and observability services. Keep public website delivery decoupled from the management platform. Use per-site identifiers and permission-scoped integrations from day one, even though launch starts with one website. Avoid claiming the stack is final until current infrastructure, hosting, data volumes and cost constraints are audited.

paragraphs.heading: SECURITY, PRIVACY, RELIABILITY AND UX QUALITY BAR
paragraphs.text: Use least-privilege RBAC, MFA for privileged users, encrypted transport and secret storage, server-side validation, rate limiting and bot protection, CSRF protection where relevant, secure session handling, tenant-isolation tests, signed webhooks, idempotency, backups and tested restoration, logging without sensitive payload leakage, monitoring and incident response. Establish privacy notices, cookie/consent controls where legally applicable, deletion/export workflows, retention schedules and minimal collection. Aim for WCAG 2.2 AA, responsive keyboard-accessible interfaces, clear empty/error/loading states, fast charts, reliable filters, and accurate time-zone/currency labeling. These are acceptance targets, not verified achievements.
DESIGN DIRECTION

paragraphs.heading: DESIGN DIRECTION
paragraphs.text: A premium editorial/SaaS hybrid: restrained palette, disciplined typography and spacing, consistent data visualization, meaningful motion, excellent contrast and mobile layouts. Navigation should prioritize Overview, Leads, Content, Analytics, SEO, Bookings, Automations, Integrations, and Settings. Primary overview answers: Where is traffic coming from? Which interactions generate qualified leads? What should I do next? Design system should be token-based, documented and reusable; avoid copying WordPress UI.

paragraphs.heading: COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE — PRIMARY-SOURCE DESCRIPTIONS, NOT INDEPENDENT PERFORMANCE PROOF
paragraphs.text: WordPress: highly flexible CMS/plugin ecosystem; not a fair feature-by-feature competitor unless website publishing is core.

paragraphs.heading: COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE — PRIMARY-SOURCE DESCRIPTIONS, NOT INDEPENDENT PERFORMANCE PROOF
paragraphs.text: Framer: visual website design/publishing; compete on business operations and integrations, not necessarily design editor quality.

paragraphs.heading: COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE — PRIMARY-SOURCE DESCRIPTIONS, NOT INDEPENDENT PERFORMANCE PROOF
paragraphs.text: Shopify: commerce-focused platform; not primary competitor for appointment-driven service firms. Do not promise superiority in ecommerce.

paragraphs.heading: COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE — PRIMARY-SOURCE DESCRIPTIONS, NOT INDEPENDENT PERFORMANCE PROOF
paragraphs.text: Other competitors for follow-up research: Wix business solutions, Squarespace Scheduling/Acuity, Zoho CRM/Bookings, Calendly, Pipedrive, HoneyBook, Dubsado, Tidio and Webflow integrations. Verify pricing and scope before quantitative matrix.
PROPOSED MARKET GAP (HYPOTHESIS TO VALIDATE)

paragraphs.heading: PROPOSED MARKET GAP (HYPOTHESIS TO VALIDATE)
paragraphs.text: Small service owners often operate website + forms + inbox + calendar + spreadsheets + analytics + task management separately. They want a trusted, low-friction way to know 'who enquired, from where, what happened next, and what should I do now?' Existing platforms cover much of this, but complexity, fragmentation, cost and setup burden may leave an underserved segment. Conduct 15-20 discovery interviews across agencies, consultants, designers and appointment-led local services; measure willingness to pay and existing spend, not just feature enthusiasm.
MVP SCOPE — FIRST SELLABLE WEDGE

paragraphs.heading: MVP SCOPE — FIRST SELLABLE WEDGE
paragraphs.text: 1\. Website connector: signed form/webhook ingest, embeddable widget/JS SDK, API keys with rotation, source/UTM capture and consent, WordPress/Framer/static/Next.js adapter recipes.

paragraphs.heading: MVP SCOPE — FIRST SELLABLE WEDGE
paragraphs.text: 2\. Unified inbox/CRM: lead timeline, dedupe, pipeline, tags, notes, follow-up tasks, lead qualification and export.

paragraphs.heading: MVP SCOPE — FIRST SELLABLE WEDGE
paragraphs.text: 3\. Appointments: booking page/widget, availability rules, timezone handling, confirmed calendar sync, reminders, double-booking prevention.

paragraphs.heading: MVP SCOPE — FIRST SELLABLE WEDGE
paragraphs.text: 4\. Simple analytics: traffic sources, landing pages, enquiry conversion, appointment and qualified-lead funnel, source attribution with caveats.

paragraphs.heading: MVP SCOPE — FIRST SELLABLE WEDGE
paragraphs.text: 5\. Sera: read and summarize real data; draft replies and content; propose changes; explicit owner approval for sends, publishes, deletions and calendar edits; complete action log.

paragraphs.heading: MVP SCOPE — FIRST SELLABLE WEDGE
paragraphs.text: 6\. Manual parity: every AI task can be completed with conventional buttons/forms; no AI requirement to operate business.

paragraphs.heading: MVP SCOPE — FIRST SELLABLE WEDGE
paragraphs.text: 7\. Accessible mobile-first admin: voice as alternative, not exclusive interaction; keyboard, screen reader, captions/transcripts, visible confirmations and undo.

paragraphs.heading: MVP SCOPE — FIRST SELLABLE WEDGE
paragraphs.text: 8\. Agency white-label baseline: logo, palette, custom domain, branded email templates and isolated customer workspaces; agency resale/billing only after demand validation.

paragraphs.heading: MVP SCOPE — FIRST SELLABLE WEDGE
paragraphs.text: OUT OF MVP: full Shopify replacement, general-purpose website builder, autonomous unsupervised agents, complex enterprise ERP, unlimited free AI inference, native integrations with every app.
DIFFERENTIATING PRODUCT IDEAS TO TEST

paragraphs.heading: DIFFERENTIATING PRODUCT IDEAS TO TEST
paragraphs.text: \- 'Explain my week' voice briefing with citations to actual lead/event records and a plain-text equivalent.

paragraphs.heading: DIFFERENTIATING PRODUCT IDEAS TO TEST

paragraphs.heading: DIFFERENTIATING PRODUCT IDEAS TO TEST

paragraphs.heading: DIFFERENTIATING PRODUCT IDEAS TO TEST

paragraphs.heading: DIFFERENTIATING PRODUCT IDEAS TO TEST
paragraphs.text: \- Outcome-first setup: 'I want more qualified consultations' configures form, booking, pipeline and measurement from one guided flow.

paragraphs.heading: DIFFERENTIATING PRODUCT IDEAS TO TEST
paragraphs.text: \- Portable data and connectors: export contacts, content and event history; no forced site migration.

paragraphs.heading: DIFFERENTIATING PRODUCT IDEAS TO TEST
paragraphs.text: \- Voice-accessible without speech dependency: text transcripts, manual editing, low-bandwidth mode, multilingual UX later.
INTEGRATION STRATEGY

paragraphs.heading: INTEGRATION STRATEGY
paragraphs.text: Start with Google Calendar, Gmail/email transport, Google Search Console, GA4 where permitted, generic webhook, WordPress, Framer and Next.js connector recipes. Then Notion and ClickUp: OAuth where supported, narrowly scoped sync for contacts/tasks/projects, conflict handling, rate limits, retry/idempotency and audit logs. Offer Zapier/Make/n8n-style webhooks where users already have automation. MCP is a secure OPTIONAL agent tool interface; it is not the transport for all website/cloud integrations. Core integrations should use REST APIs, OAuth, signed webhooks and event contracts. Provide per-tenant scopes and approval policies; prohibit cross-tenant data access. Future MCP server can expose read_leads, summarize_traffic, draft_followup, propose_booking and approval-gated execute actions. Confirm exact APIs and platform rules before implementation.
ARCHITECTURE AND WHITE-LABEL REQUIREMENTS

paragraphs.heading: ARCHITECTURE AND WHITE-LABEL REQUIREMENTS
paragraphs.text: Multi-tenant organization/site/account model; strict isolation, RBAC, domain and brand configuration, themes/tokens, localized timezone/currency, feature flags, API/webhook management, queue/outbox, audit logs, backup/restore, data portability, consent and retention controls. Single-owner UI hides agency complexity. Secure service-to-service auth, signed webhooks, encryption, idempotency and rate limiting. Accessibility target WCAG 2.2 AA with tested voice and manual workflows. Separate tenant domains and certificate provisioning. Distinguish control-plane (agency configuration) from data-plane (tenant leads/content/events).
BUSINESS MODEL / UNIT ECONOMICS — HYPOTHESES

paragraphs.heading: BUSINESS MODEL / UNIT ECONOMICS — HYPOTHESES
paragraphs.text: Personal-use and pilot may target zero NEW subscription cost using existing hosting and free tools, but a commercial multi-tenant SaaS cannot responsibly promise zero hosting, email, support, security or AI costs. Model infrastructure per tenant, AI inference per request, storage, messages, integration quotas, support hours and gross margin. Potential tiers: Starter (manual CRM, forms, booking), Growth (attribution, automations, limited AI), Agency (white-label, multiple sites, client workspaces). Do not set prices before interviews, competitor validation and cost model. Meter expensive AI/voice separately and offer opt-in BYO provider where appropriate.
GO-TO-MARKET AND VALIDATION

paragraphs.heading: GO-TO-MARKET AND VALIDATION
paragraphs.text: Stage 0: use Hadi portfolio as internal design partner; fix booking reliability and tracking before external promise.

paragraphs.heading: GO-TO-MARKET AND VALIDATION
paragraphs.text: Stage 1: interview 15-20 service owners; select one niche (e.g., boutique creative agencies and independent consultants).

paragraphs.heading: GO-TO-MARKET AND VALIDATION
paragraphs.text: Stage 2: prototype 3 journeys: connect existing site in <30 minutes (target), capture first lead, turn lead into confirmed appointment; Sera propose-and-approve follow-up.

paragraphs.heading: GO-TO-MARKET AND VALIDATION
paragraphs.text: Stage 3: invite 5-10 pilot businesses; measure activation, time to first lead, lead loss, appointment completion, weekly active owner usage, retention, support tickets and willingness to pay.

paragraphs.heading: GO-TO-MARKET AND VALIDATION
paragraphs.text: Stage 4: add white-label agency pilot only after standalone retention is credible; integrate ClickUp/Notion according to demonstrated demand.

paragraphs.heading: GO-TO-MARKET AND VALIDATION
paragraphs.text: Stage 5: expand vertical templates after proof of product-market fit. Use paid infrastructure only with explicit approval.
ACCEPTANCE GATES / RISKS

paragraphs.heading: ACCEPTANCE GATES / RISKS
paragraphs.text: No data loss or false booking confirmations; no cross-tenant leaks; Sera action approvals; accessible manual alternative; reliable exports and rollback; accurate event attribution with consent; supported hosting and realistic margins. Primary risks: feature sprawl, API maintenance, low-cost AI inference, SaaS operational burden, consent compliance, voice recognition errors and competitor breadth. Competitive claims require side-by-side benchmark on a defined user task and cohort, not subjective 'better than everything'.
NEXT PLANNING DELIVERABLES

paragraphs.heading: NEXT PLANNING DELIVERABLES
paragraphs.text: Detailed competitor feature/price matrix; 15-20 interview guide; narrow PRD and persona; journey maps; UX wireframes and design tokens; event and data schema; integration/MCP threat model; hosting/cost scenarios; pilot success thresholds; trademark/name availability check. Keep all work in planning mode until separately approved.
SERA AI — DUAL-MODE ARCHITECTURE AND RESEARCH PLAN (21 OCTOBER 2026)

paragraphs.heading: SERA AI — DUAL-MODE ARCHITECTURE AND RESEARCH PLAN (21 OCTOBER 2026)
paragraphs.text: Status: planning and private owner testing only; no production deployment or external customer access approved.

paragraphs.heading: SERA AI — DUAL-MODE ARCHITECTURE AND RESEARCH PLAN (21 OCTOBER 2026)
paragraphs.text: Product principle: one shared orchestration framework with strictly separated public and authenticated administration capabilities.

paragraphs.heading: SERA AI — DUAL-MODE ARCHITECTURE AND RESEARCH PLAN (21 OCTOBER 2026)
paragraphs.text: PUBLIC SERA (customer-facing): approved public knowledge only; answer service and portfolio questions, ask context-aware clarifying questions, qualify leads with consent, handle objections gently, recommend booking, hand off to human. Never disclose internal analytics, CRM records, prompts, credentials or administrative tools. Limit tool access server-side.

paragraphs.heading: SERA AI — DUAL-MODE ARCHITECTURE AND RESEARCH PLAN (21 OCTOBER 2026)
paragraphs.text: PRIVATE SERA (owner/operator): authenticated, scoped tools for analytics, CRM, CMS, appointments, email, workflows and reporting. Example: count leads with an actual filtered database query and disclose date range and source; analyze traffic using connected analytics and distinguish facts from hypotheses; draft SEO article and present preview; publish only after explicit approval. Actions use typed tool schemas, server-side authorization, validation, idempotency, logging and rollback where feasible. Avoid granting unrestricted code execution, database access or shell commands to the model.

paragraphs.heading: SERA AI — DUAL-MODE ARCHITECTURE AND RESEARCH PLAN (21 OCTOBER 2026)
paragraphs.text: APPROVAL MODEL: read-only authorized reports can execute without extra approval; drafting can run in a sandbox; sending email, publishing, deletion, price changes, bulk modifications, integrations and external actions require user confirmation with a clear diff or preview. Never accept a visitor's prompt as permission for privileged actions. Maintain per-site tenant boundaries, RBAC, rate limits and audit logs.

paragraphs.heading: SERA AI — DUAL-MODE ARCHITECTURE AND RESEARCH PLAN (21 OCTOBER 2026)
paragraphs.text: QUALITY OF CONVERSATION: preserve session context and business-specific knowledge with retrieval; ask one useful follow-up at a time, handle interruptions, objections, multilingual speech and cross-questioning; clarify unknowns instead of inventing figures or promises. Measure task completion, factual grounding, handoff rate, response time and satisfaction; build a repeatable evaluation set with adversarial prompt-injection tests.

paragraphs.heading: SERA AI — DUAL-MODE ARCHITECTURE AND RESEARCH PLAN (21 OCTOBER 2026)
paragraphs.text: MULTI-MODEL ROUTING: configurable model adapter registry, primary Gemini Flash and optional additional permitted free-tier providers; health checks, quota accounting, budget caps, per-request model selection, circuit breakers and graceful fallback. Do not promise unlimited free inference, evade provider limits or assume commercial use is permitted by a free tier. Keep provider keys server-side. Switching models must preserve relevant authorized context without leaking confidential data across providers. Verify provider terms, rate limits and privacy before activation.

paragraphs.heading: SERA AI — DUAL-MODE ARCHITECTURE AND RESEARCH PLAN (21 OCTOBER 2026)
paragraphs.text: VOICE: progressive enhancement with text-first parity, microphone consent, captions, push-to-talk, interruptions and accessible keyboard fallback. Browser speech APIs vary by browser, may rely on third-party processing and do not guarantee zero cost or privacy; test before choosing speech-to-text and text-to-speech infrastructure. Never claim voice can perform an action without a confirmed backend tool result.

paragraphs.heading: SERA AI — DUAL-MODE ARCHITECTURE AND RESEARCH PLAN (21 OCTOBER 2026)
paragraphs.text: HOSTING: Hostinger Business Web Hosting capability matrix remains unverified. Confirm supported runtimes, background jobs, database capacity, cron, resource limits and network access before committing to a deployment design. Favor a modular lightweight backend; avoid promising persistent local LLM inference on shared hosting.

paragraphs.heading: SERA AI — DUAL-MODE ARCHITECTURE AND RESEARCH PLAN (21 OCTOBER 2026)
paragraphs.text: OWNER-ONLY PILOT: (1) read-only lead count and traffic source reports; (2) CRM follow-up suggestions; (3) article draft and preview; (4) approval-gated publishing; (5) voice interface evaluation; (6) multi-provider failover under real quota limits. Define acceptance tests for authorization, data correctness, latency, accessibility, prompt injection, cross-tenant isolation, failure recovery and logging. No public launch until tests pass.

paragraphs.heading: SERA AI — DUAL-MODE ARCHITECTURE AND RESEARCH PLAN (21 OCTOBER 2026)
paragraphs.text: RESEARCH VALIDATION BACKLOG: verify current official Gemini API free-tier policies, alternative provider terms, OpenAI/Anthropic guidance on tool execution and prompt injection, OWASP LLM Top 10, WCAG 2.2, MCP authorization/security specifications and Hostinger plan capabilities. This section is a design proposal, not a claim that live APIs or hosting limits have been verified.
PRODUCT BLUEPRINT REFINEMENT — CONNECT-FIRST, EXTENSIBLE-BY-DESIGN (21 OCT 2026)

paragraphs.heading: PRODUCT BLUEPRINT REFINEMENT — CONNECT-FIRST, EXTENSIBLE-BY-DESIGN (21 OCT 2026)
paragraphs.text: DECISION: Build the first release as an integration layer for existing service websites, not a website builder. Hadi's portfolio is the private pilot. Preserve future white-label, multi-site and MCP extensibility through interfaces and data boundaries from day one; do not implement every enterprise feature now. Planning only.

paragraphs.heading: PRODUCT BLUEPRINT REFINEMENT — CONNECT-FIRST, EXTENSIBLE-BY-DESIGN (21 OCT 2026)
paragraphs.text: PRODUCT OUTCOME: Visitor -> consented enquiry -> qualified lead -> reliable booking -> owner follow-up -> won/lost outcome. Core system works without AI. Primary initial persona: independent service professional / small creative agency; other industries remain future validation targets.

paragraphs.heading: PRODUCT BLUEPRINT REFINEMENT — CONNECT-FIRST, EXTENSIBLE-BY-DESIGN (21 OCT 2026)
paragraphs.text: NON-NEGOTIABLE DESIGN RULES: modular monolith first; documented contracts; provider adapters for analytics, calendar, email, AI and CMS; tenant_id and site_id on owned records from the beginning; authorization on every read/write; stable IDs and timestamps; event/outbox mechanism for reliable integrations; audit events and idempotent retries; migrations with backward compatibility; configuration rather than per-customer code forks. Design for extraction later, but do not prematurely deploy microservices.

paragraphs.heading: PRODUCT BLUEPRINT REFINEMENT — CONNECT-FIRST, EXTENSIBLE-BY-DESIGN (21 OCT 2026)
paragraphs.text: WHITE-LABEL EXTENSION SEAMS: organization -> workspace -> site hierarchy, configurable logo/name/colors/domain/email sender, design tokens, localization/time zone, templates, feature entitlements and permission policies. Build a single-owner UI first; store configurations so agency views can be added without data migration. Brand theming must not override accessibility or security controls.

paragraphs.heading: PRODUCT BLUEPRINT REFINEMENT — CONNECT-FIRST, EXTENSIBLE-BY-DESIGN (21 OCT 2026)
paragraphs.text: INTEGRATION CONTRACT: signed, versioned webhooks and documented REST APIs for ordinary websites; lightweight JS snippet or hosted forms for leads; WordPress/Framer/custom-site adapters as demand validates. MCP is an optional tool interface for AI assistants, not a replacement for APIs, webhooks or OAuth. Use least-privilege scopes, token rotation, replay prevention, bounded retries, dead-letter handling and per-site rate limits. Never put credentials in client-side scripts.

paragraphs.heading: PRODUCT BLUEPRINT REFINEMENT — CONNECT-FIRST, EXTENSIBLE-BY-DESIGN (21 OCT 2026)
paragraphs.text: FIRST RELEASE MODULES: dashboard with actionable next steps; contacts and deduplicated leads; pipeline stages and notes; secure lead forms with spam protection and consent; reliable booking with provider event confirmation, time-zone handling and conflict checks; basic source/UTM attribution and analytics integration; simple content editing for own site via adapter; public Sera and private read-only Sera reporting with citations to live records. AI writes/publishing follow after approval flows are tested. Do not invent traffic or lead figures when data sources are disconnected.

paragraphs.heading: PRODUCT BLUEPRINT REFINEMENT — CONNECT-FIRST, EXTENSIBLE-BY-DESIGN (21 OCT 2026)
paragraphs.text: EXPLICIT NON-GOALS FOR MVP: drag-and-drop site builder, ecommerce, full marketing automation suite, autonomous price negotiation, marketplace of connectors, general-purpose workflow builder, unlimited AI, multi-region enterprise hosting and all-industry templates. Keep future extension points without shipping these features.

paragraphs.heading: PRODUCT BLUEPRINT REFINEMENT — CONNECT-FIRST, EXTENSIBLE-BY-DESIGN (21 OCT 2026)
paragraphs.text: UX STANDARD: voice and keyboard/mouse parity; clear information hierarchy; fast search and global command palette; quick actions, undo and activity history; empty/loading/error states; onboarding with guided first lead and test booking; accessible forms and charts; mobile owner workflows. Evaluate against WCAG 2.2 AA, real task usability tests and measured Core Web Vitals rather than aesthetic claims alone.

paragraphs.heading: PRODUCT BLUEPRINT REFINEMENT — CONNECT-FIRST, EXTENSIBLE-BY-DESIGN (21 OCT 2026)
paragraphs.text: SECURITY/RELIABILITY STANDARD: OWASP ASVS and API Security Top 10 as verification references, OWASP LLM risks for Sera; session hardening, CSRF where applicable, server validation, RBAC and tenant isolation tests, encrypted secrets, data retention/export/deletion, backups and restore drills, monitoring and incident runbooks. Verify privacy/consent obligations in actual target jurisdictions. Use privacy-preserving analytics and avoid sensitive data in model prompts or logs.

paragraphs.heading: PRODUCT BLUEPRINT REFINEMENT — CONNECT-FIRST, EXTENSIBLE-BY-DESIGN (21 OCT 2026)
paragraphs.text: ENGINEERING QUALITY GATES: CI lint/type/unit/integration/e2e checks; contract tests for adapters; automated booking reconciliation; migrations with rollback plan; staging environment; observability for failed jobs and webhook deliveries; documented SLO targets established after baseline measurement. Test prompt injection, hallucinated action completion, provider outages and approval bypass. Do not claim '100% secure' or Awwwards-level performance without independent evidence.

paragraphs.heading: PRODUCT BLUEPRINT REFINEMENT — CONNECT-FIRST, EXTENSIBLE-BY-DESIGN (21 OCT 2026)
paragraphs.text: MEASUREMENT: activation (site connected and first test lead captured), valid lead capture rate, lead-to-booked conversion, no-show and booking failure rate, response latency, Sera grounded-answer accuracy, action approval success, owner time saved, weekly active usage, retention, per-site operating cost. Establish baselines and targets during pilot rather than fabricate them.

paragraphs.heading: PRODUCT BLUEPRINT REFINEMENT — CONNECT-FIRST, EXTENSIBLE-BY-DESIGN (21 OCT 2026)
paragraphs.text: PHASE GATES: 0) audit existing portfolio CRM, calendar, Sera and hosting; resolve broken booking before expanding. 1) private connect-first MVP and manual-first workflows. 2) private Sera reporting, drafts and approval-gated actions. 3) validate integrations and five external pilots only with approval. 4) configurable white-label pilot and broader connector SDK after retention proof. 5) consider website building only if demand and economics justify it.

paragraphs.heading: PRODUCT BLUEPRINT REFINEMENT — CONNECT-FIRST, EXTENSIBLE-BY-DESIGN (21 OCT 2026)
paragraphs.text: DOCUMENT GOVERNANCE: maintain a single PRD, architecture decision records (ADR), requirements traceability, risk register, acceptance criteria, and a decision log with 'confirmed / assumption / needs verification' labels. Existing planning sections are historical research; this decision supersedes any earlier recommendation to build a full website builder immediately. No code or deployment authorized.

paragraphs.heading: VERSIONED DELIVERY ROADMAP — APPROVED PLANNING ORDER (21 OCTOBER 2026)

paragraphs.heading: VERSIONED DELIVERY ROADMAP — APPROVED PLANNING ORDER (21 OCTOBER 2026)

paragraphs.heading: VERSIONED DELIVERY ROADMAP — APPROVED PLANNING ORDER (21 OCTOBER 2026)
paragraphs.text: V1.1+ — WHITE-LABEL / AGENCY: custom branding/domains, organization/site workspaces, roles, agency management, reusable templates and multi-site reporting; build on V0.2 tenancy/configuration foundations. Gate: no cross-tenant access and validated demand.

paragraphs.heading: VERSIONED DELIVERY ROADMAP — APPROVED PLANNING ORDER (21 OCTOBER 2026)

Full website builder, ecommerce and broad industry coverage remain optional future products, not commitments.

paragraphs.heading: VERSIONED DELIVERY ROADMAP — APPROVED PLANNING ORDER (21 OCTOBER 2026)

paragraphs.heading: VERSIONED DELIVERY ROADMAP — APPROVED PLANNING ORDER (21 OCTOBER 2026)
